9-1.bio:
September 1 marks the Indiction, the beginning of the Ecclesiastical New Year. The custom derives from the civil calendar of the Roman Empire, in which the yearly cycle of taxation and public life began in September, and the Church took up this reckoning for her own cycle of feasts.

On this day the Church prays for God's blessing upon the new year, remembering that Christ read in the synagogue at Nazareth the words of Isaiah, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me... to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord." It is also kept in our time as a day of prayer for the protection of the natural environment.
9-1.desc: The Indiction — beginning of the Ecclesiastical New Year.
9-1.name: Beginning of the Church Year

9-1.bio:
St. Simeon Stylites the Elder was a Syrian ascetic of the fifth century who, seeking greater stillness, took up his dwelling on top of a pillar near Antioch. There he stood for many years in prayer and fasting, teaching the crowds who gathered below and reconciling enemies, until his repose in the year 459.

He was the first and most famous of the pillar-dwellers, and his extraordinary endurance made him a wonder of the Christian world even in his lifetime. He is commemorated on September 1, at the opening of the church year.
9-1.desc: Venerable Symeon Stylites the Elder who stood 36 years on a pillar.
9-1.name: Simeon Stylites the Elder

9-1.bio:
The 40 Holy Virgins were ascetic women of Thrace who, with their teacher Ammon the Deacon, confessed Christ during the persecution under Licinius in the early fourth century. Refusing to sacrifice to idols, they endured imprisonment and torture with their teacher, and received together the crown of martyrdom at Heraclea in Thrace.

Greek tradition preserves their forty names — among them Ourania, Aspasia, Penelope, Margarita, Erato, Kleio, and Melpomeni — and on September 1 women bearing these names celebrate their name day. The holy virgins and St. Ammon are honored as examples of steadfast faith at the very opening of the church year.
9-1.desc: The 40 Holy Ascetic Virgin Martyrs of Thrace and their teacher Ammon the Deacon.
9-1.name: 40 Holy Virgin Martyrs of Thrace

9-1.bio:
The righteous Joshua, son of Nun, was the servant and successor of the Prophet Moses. He was one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan and, with Caleb, alone trusted that God would give the land to His people. After the death of Moses he led Israel across the Jordan, took Jericho, and divided the land among the tribes.

The Church honors him as a type of Christ, whose name he bears in its Greek form, and remembers his vision of the Captain of the Lord's host before Jericho. His memory is kept on September 1, the beginning of the Church year.
9-1.desc: Righteous Joshua the son of Nun, successor of Moses and leader of Israel into the Promised Land.
9-1.name: Joshua the Son of Nun

9-1.bio:
St. Martha was the mother of St. Simeon the Stylite of the Wonderful Mountain, the younger stylite, and lived in the region of Antioch. A woman of great humility and constant prayer, she raised her son in piety and later lived near his pillar, serving the poor and the sick who came to him.

Tradition relates that she was warned of her death in a vision and reposed in peace; her son and his disciples honored her memory with a church. She is commemorated on September 1, alongside the great stylite Simeon the Elder.
9-1.desc: Venerable Martha, mother of St. Simeon Stylites of the Wonderful Mountain.
9-1.name: Martha the Mother of Simeon Stylites

9-1.bio:
The venerable Evanthia is listed in the Greek Synaxarion on September 1 among the righteous who reposed in peace. Little is recorded of her life beyond her name, which means a fair flowering, and the tradition that she lived in holiness and prayer.

Her memory is kept especially in Greece, where Evanthia remains a living baptismal name and this day is celebrated as her name day.
9-1.desc: Venerable Evanthia, righteous woman commemorated at the opening of the Church year.
9-1.name: Evanthia the Righteous

9-1.bio:
St. Meletios the New was born in Cappadocia in the eleventh century and came as a young man to Greece, where he embraced the monastic life. He settled on Mount Myoupolis near Thebes, in the region of Kithairon, and founded a monastery that drew many disciples.

He was known for his foolishness for Christ, his plain preaching, and his charity toward the poor, and was honored by emperors of his day. He reposed in peace in the early twelfth century and is commemorated on September 1.
9-1.desc: Venerable Meletios the New, ascetic of Mount Myoupolis in Boeotia.
9-1.name: Meletios the New of Myoupolis

9-1.bio:
The holy martyrs Evodos, Kallisti and Hermogenes were siblings who confessed Christ at Nicomedia during the persecutions of the early fourth century. Refusing to offer sacrifice to idols, they were condemned and beheaded together.

The Church commemorates them on September 1 together with the Forty Virgin Martyrs of Adrianople.
9-1.desc: Holy Martyrs Evodos, Kallisti and Hermogenes, siblings of Nicomedia.
9-1.name: Evodos, Kallisti and Hermogenes

9-1.bio:
St. Angelis was a goldsmith of Constantinople in the seventeenth century. Tradition relates that, having once in a moment of weakness been counted among the Muslims, he repented and openly confessed himself a Christian before the Ottoman authorities.

Refusing every inducement to deny Christ, he was condemned and beheaded in Constantinople in 1680. The Church commemorates him on September 1.
9-1.desc: New Martyr Angelis, goldsmith of Constantinople, martyred under the Ottomans.
9-1.name: Angelis the New Martyr of Constantinople

9-10.bio:
St. Pulcheria was a Byzantine empress of the fifth century, sister of the Emperor Theodosius II. She took a vow of virginity, guided the empire with wisdom and piety, and was a steadfast defender of the Orthodox faith, laboring for the Fourth Ecumenical Council at Chalcedon which confessed Christ as true God and true man.

She built churches in honor of the Theotokos in Constantinople and used her rank in the service of the Church and the poor. She is commemorated on September 10.
9-10.name: Pulcheria

9-10.bio:
The holy virgins Menodora, Metrodora and Nymphodora were sisters of Bithynia who withdrew to a solitary place near the hot springs of Pythia to live in prayer and virginity. Denounced to the governor Fronto in the persecution of the early fourth century, they were tortured one after another before each other's eyes and put to death, refusing to deny Christ.

Their relics were laid to rest together, and they are commemorated on September 10.
9-10.desc: Holy Virgin Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora and Nymphodora, sisters of Bithynia.
9-10.name: Menodora, Metrodora and Nymphodora

9-10.bio:
St. Barypsabas was a hermit of the East who, tradition relates, was entrusted with a vessel containing the precious blood of the Savior gathered at the Crucifixion, by which many miracles of healing were worked. He carried it to Dalmatia, where he was killed by robbers for its sake.

He is commemorated on September 10.
9-10.name: Barypsabas the Martyr

9-10.bio:
St. Peter was bishop of Nicaea in the ninth century and suffered for the veneration of the holy icons under the iconoclast emperors, standing firm as a confessor. St. Paul, likewise bishop of Nicaea, is remembered for his holy life and his defense of Orthodoxy.

Both reposed in peace and are commemorated together on September 10.
9-10.desc: Sts. Peter and Paul, bishops of Nicaea and confessors of the holy icons.
9-10.name: Peter and Paul of Nicaea

9-10.bio:
The holy apostles Apelles, Luke and Clement are numbered among the Seventy. Apelles, whom the Apostle Paul calls approved in Christ, is said to have been bishop of Heraclea; Luke, or Lucius, kinsman of Paul, bishop of Laodicea in Syria; and Clement, whose name Paul writes is in the book of life, bishop of Sardis.

They are commemorated together on September 10.
9-10.desc: Holy Apostles Apelles, Luke and Clement of the Seventy.
9-10.name: Apelles, Luke and Clement the Apostles

9-10.bio:
St. Isaiah was a hermit of the Troodos mountains of Cyprus in the eleventh century. Tradition relates that the Byzantine governor Manuel Boutomites, healed through his prayers, obtained for him from the emperor Alexios Komnenos the icon of the Theotokos painted by St. Luke, around which he founded the monastery of Kykkos.

Kykkos remains the most venerated monastery of Cyprus. St. Isaiah is commemorated on September 10.
9-10.desc: Venerable Isaiah, hermit and founder of the Kykkos Monastery in Cyprus.
9-10.name: Isaiah of Kykkos

9-11.bio:
St. Theodora of Alexandria lived in the fifth century. Having fallen into sin, she was seized with deep repentance and, disguising herself in men's clothing, entered a monastery under the name of the monk Theodore, where she labored for years in humility, obedience, and secret tears, patiently bearing even false accusation.

Only after her repose was her identity revealed, and the brethren marveled at the depth of her repentance. She is honored as a model of contrition and hidden struggle, and is commemorated on September 11.
9-11.name: Theodora of Alexandria

9-11.bio:
St. Euphrosynos was a simple monk of peasant birth who served as cook in his monastery, bearing the scorn of the brethren with patience and hidden prayer. Tradition relates that a priest of the monastery saw him in a dream standing in Paradise and received from him three apples, which he found beside his bed when he awoke.

When the vision became known, Euphrosynos fled the monastery to escape human praise. He is commemorated on September 11.
9-11.desc: Venerable Euphrosynos the Cook, humble monk who was shown in Paradise.
9-11.name: Euphrosynos the Cook

9-11.bio:
St. Demetrios was prince and governor of Skepsis on the Hellespont, converted to Christ with his wife Evanthia and their son Demetrianos by the preaching of St. Cornelius the Centurion. Tradition relates that, when a new pagan governor arrived, the family confessed the faith and were put to death for it.

They are commemorated together on September 11.
9-11.desc: Holy Martyrs Demetrios, his wife Evanthia and their son Demetrianos of Skepsis.
9-11.name: Demetrios, Evanthia and Demetrianos of Skepsis

9-11.bio:
The holy martyrs Diodoros, Diomedes and Didymos were Christians of Laodicea in Syria who confessed Christ during the pagan persecutions and were flogged to death.

They are commemorated on September 11.
9-11.desc: Holy Martyrs Diodoros, Diomedes and Didymos of Laodicea.
9-11.name: Diodoros, Diomedes and Didymos

9-11.bio:
St. Theodora of Vasta lived in the Peloponnese in the Byzantine period and, tradition relates, disguised herself as a man to serve as a soldier in place of her aged father. Falsely accused and condemned, she prayed that her body might become a church, her hair trees and her blood a spring, and was put to death.

At Vasta in Arcadia a small chapel dedicated to her bears seventeen large trees growing from its roof, with a spring beneath, and is a place of pilgrimage. She is commemorated on September 11.
9-11.desc: Holy Martyr Theodora of Vasta in Arcadia, whose chapel bears trees on its roof.
9-11.name: Theodora of Vasta

9-11.bio:
St. Elias the Cave-dweller was born at Reggio in Calabria in the ninth century and embraced the ascetic life in the caves of southern Italy, then part of the Byzantine world, together with his companion Arsenios. He was known for his humility, his gift of discernment, and the many disciples he guided.

He reposed in the early tenth century and is commemorated with Arsenios on September 11.
9-11.desc: Venerable Elias the Cave-dweller of Calabria and his disciple Arsenios.
9-11.name: Elias the Cave-dweller and Arsenios

9-11.bio:
St. Ia was a Christian woman taken captive with a great multitude of believers by the Persian king Shapur II in the fourth century. Refusing to renounce Christ, she endured prolonged torture and was beheaded.

She is commemorated on September 11 with the many who suffered with her.
9-11.desc: Holy Martyr Ia of Persia and the many Christians martyred with her.
9-11.name: Ia of Persia and the 9,000 with her

9-12.bio:
St. Autonomos was a bishop from Italy who, during the persecution under Diocletian, came to Bithynia in Asia Minor, where he preached the Gospel and brought many pagans to faith in Christ. He was slain by a pagan mob while serving the Divine Liturgy, offering his own life together with the bloodless sacrifice.

He is honored as a hieromartyr whose zeal for the Gospel carried him far from his homeland. He is commemorated on September 12.
9-12.name: Autonomous

9-12.bio:
St. Kournoutos was bishop of Iconium in Asia Minor who suffered during the persecutions of the third century under the governor Perennius. Refusing to deny Christ, he was tortured and beheaded.

He is commemorated on September 12.
9-12.name: Kournoutos of Iconium

9-12.bio:
St. Julian was a priest of Ancyra in Galatia who, during the persecution of the early fourth century, hid with forty Christians in a cave and celebrated the divine services there. Betrayed to the authorities, they were seized while at prayer and, refusing to sacrifice to idols, were all put to death.

They are commemorated on September 12.
9-12.desc: Hieromartyr Julian, presbyter of Ancyra in Galatia, and forty martyrs with him.
9-12.name: Julian of Ancyra and the 40 with him

9-12.bio:
St. Theodore was bishop of Alexandria who was seized by the pagans in the time of the persecutions, crowned with thorns in mockery of the Savior, and thrown into the sea. Tradition relates that he was preserved unharmed and was then beheaded.

He is commemorated on September 12.
9-12.name: Theodore of Alexandria

9-12.bio:
The holy martyrs Macedonius, Theodoulos and Tatian were Christians of Phrygia who, in the reign of Julian the Apostate, refused to take part in pagan sacrifices and were burned to death on an iron grill.

They are commemorated on September 12.
9-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Macedonius, Theodoulos and Tatian of Phrygia.
9-12.name: Macedonius, Theodoulos and Tatian

9-12.bio:
St. Daniel of Thasos was an ascetic who lived in prayer and solitude on the island of Thasos in the northern Aegean. Tradition relates that he was a man of great humility and reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 12.
9-12.desc: Venerable Daniel of Thasos, ascetic of the island.
9-12.name: Daniel of Thasos

9-12.bio:
St. Andronikos was a monk of Atroa on the slopes of the Bithynian Olympus, a great center of monastic life in the Byzantine period. He lived in asceticism and prayer and reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 12.
9-12.desc: Venerable Andronikos, ascetic of Atroa in Bithynia.
9-12.name: Andronikos of Atroa

9-13.bio:
St. Cornelius was a Roman centurion stationed at Caesarea, a devout man who feared God, gave alms generously, and prayed continually. As the Acts of the Apostles relates, an angel directed him to send for the Apostle Peter, and he and his household became the first Gentiles to be baptized into Christ.

Tradition holds that he afterward labored in the preaching of the Gospel and served the Church as a bishop. He is commemorated on September 13.
9-13.name: Kornelios the Centurion

9-13.bio:
St. Aristides was a philosopher of Athens in the second century who, after coming to faith in Christ, addressed a written defense of the Christians to the emperor Hadrian, and tradition relates a second to Antoninus Pius. His Apology, rediscovered in modern times, is among the earliest surviving defenses of the faith, setting Christian worship of the one Creator against the errors of the pagans and describing the pure life of the Christians.

Tradition holds that he sealed his witness with martyrdom at Athens. He is commemorated on September 13, a name day for Aristides and Aristea.
9-13.desc: Holy Martyr Aristides the Philosopher of Athens, apologist of the faith.
9-13.name: Aristides the Philosopher

9-13.bio:
After St. Helen found the True Cross, the emperor Constantine the Great built a great church over the tomb of Christ and the hill of Golgotha in Jerusalem. Its dedication was celebrated in the year 335 with a gathering of bishops from across the empire, and the Exaltation of the Cross was appointed for the following day.

The Church keeps the memory of this dedication each year on September 13, on the eve of the Exaltation.
9-13.desc: Commemoration of the dedication of the Church of the Resurrection, the Holy Sepulchre, in Jerusalem.
9-13.name: Founding of the Church of the Resurrection

9-13.bio:
The holy martyrs Chronides, Leontios and Serapion were Christians of Alexandria who confessed Christ in the persecution of the third century. Tradition relates that after torments they were cast into the sea and that their bodies were recovered and buried by the faithful.

They are commemorated on September 13.
9-13.desc: Holy Martyrs Chronides, Leontios and Serapion of Alexandria.
9-13.name: Chronides, Leontios and Serapion

9-13.bio:
St. Meletios Pigas was born in Crete in the sixteenth century and studied at Padua before embracing the monastic life. As Patriarch of Alexandria from 1590 he labored to strengthen the Orthodox of Egypt and, as locum tenens of Constantinople, defended the Church against Latin and Protestant pressures and against the new calendar of Rome.

A learned theologian and preacher, he reposed in 1601 and is commemorated on September 13.
9-13.desc: St. Meletios Pigas, Patriarch of Alexandria, theologian and defender of Orthodoxy.
9-13.name: Meletios Pigas of Alexandria

9-13.bio:
St. Hierotheos was born at Kalamata in 1686 and, after studies in Constantinople, came to Mount Athos, where he was tonsured at the monastery of Iveron. A learned man, he later taught and preached in Venice and the Ionian islands before returning to the Holy Mountain to live in asceticism.

He reposed in 1745 on the island of Youra, and his relics were brought to Iveron. He is commemorated on September 13.
9-13.desc: Venerable Hierotheos the Younger of Kalamata, monk of Iveron on Mount Athos.
9-13.name: Hierotheos the Younger of Iveron

9-13.bio:
St. Chrysostomos was Metropolitan of Smyrna in the years of the Asia Minor catastrophe. Refusing to abandon his flock when the Turkish army entered the city in September 1922, he was handed over to a mob and killed. With him the Church honors the hierarchs Gregory of Kydonies, Ambrose of Moschonisia, Prokopios of Ikonion and Euthymios of Zela, who were martyred in the same days, together with the clergy and laity who died with them.

They were glorified by the Church of Greece in 1992 and are commemorated on September 13.
9-13.desc: Hieromartyr Chrysostomos of Smyrna and the bishops martyred with him in the Asia Minor catastrophe of 1922.
9-13.name: Chrysostomos of Smyrna and the Hierarchs with him

9-14.bio:
The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross commemorates the finding of the true Cross of Christ in Jerusalem by St. Helen, mother of St. Constantine the Great, in the fourth century. The Cross was raised aloft by the Patriarch before the people, who bowed down crying out for mercy. The feast also recalls the return of the Cross to Jerusalem from Persian captivity in the seventh century.

Kept on September 14 as a strict fast day in reverence for the Passion, the feast celebrates the Cross as the weapon of victory over death. It is the name day of Stavros and Stavroula.
9-14.desc: The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross.
9-14.name: Exaltation of the Holy Cross

9-14.bio:
St. Aelia Flaccilla, called Plakilla in Greek, was the wife of the emperor Theodosius the Great in the fourth century. She was known for her Orthodox faith and her humility, personally serving the sick and the poor in the hospitals of Constantinople, and St. Gregory of Nyssa delivered her funeral oration.

She reposed around 386 and is commemorated on September 14.
9-14.desc: Righteous Plakilla, empress, wife of Theodosius the Great.
9-14.name: Plakilla the Empress

9-14.bio:
The Sixth Ecumenical Council met in Constantinople in 680 and 681 under the emperor Constantine IV. It condemned the Monothelite heresy, which taught that Christ had only one will, and confirmed that He has two natural wills and two energies, divine and human, without division or confusion.

The Holy Fathers of the Council are commemorated on September 14.
9-14.desc: Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the Sixth Ecumenical Council in Constantinople.
9-14.name: Fathers of the Sixth Ecumenical Council

9-14.bio:
St. Papas was a Christian of Lycaonia in Asia Minor who confessed Christ during the pagan persecutions. Tradition relates that he was forced to walk in shoes fitted with nails and was bound to a tree, where he gave up his soul.

He is commemorated on September 14.
9-14.name: Papas the Martyr

9-14.bio:
St. Makarios was born in Thessaloniki and became a monk at the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos, a disciple of St. Niphon, Patriarch of Constantinople. With his elder's blessing he went to Thessaloniki, where he openly preached Christ before the Turks and was beheaded in 1527.

Tradition relates that St. Niphon knew of his martyrdom on Athos at the hour it took place. He is commemorated on September 14.
9-14.desc: New Martyr Makarios of Thessaloniki, monk of Dionysiou and disciple of St. Niphon.
9-14.name: Makarios the New of Thessaloniki

9-14.bio:
St. Gerasimos was an ascetic of the seventeenth century who founded the monastery of the Holy Trinity at Sourvia, near Makrinitsa on Mount Pelion in Thessaly, and guided its brotherhood in the monastic life. He reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 14.
9-14.desc: Venerable Gerasimos, founder of the Monastery of the Holy Trinity of Sourvia on Pelion.
9-14.name: Gerasimos of Sourvia

9-15.bio:
St. Nikitas the Great Martyr was a Goth living beyond the Danube in the fourth century. Converted to Christ, he confessed the faith boldly among his own people, and when a persecution arose against the Christians of that land he was seized, tortured, and given over to death by fire around the year 372.

His relics were reverently recovered by a friend and became a source of blessing to the faithful. Widely venerated in Greece, where his name means victor, he is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.name: Nikitas the Great Martyr

9-15.bio:
St. Philotheos was a married priest of a village in Bithynia in the tenth century, a man of prayer, fasting and generous charity. Tradition relates that he was granted the gift of working miracles in his lifetime, and that after his repose a healing myrrh flowed from his relics.

He is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.desc: Venerable Philotheos the Presbyter and Wonderworker of Bithynia.
9-15.name: Philotheos the Presbyter

9-15.bio:
St. Bessarion was born near Trikala in Thessaly in the fifteenth century and became Metropolitan of Larissa, a shepherd known for his charity, for ransoming captives, and for building bridges and roads for the poor of his region. He founded the monastery of Dousikou near Pyli, which still bears his name.

He reposed in 1540 and is commemorated on September 15, a name day for Vissarion.
9-15.desc: St. Bessarion, Archbishop of Larissa, founder of the Dousikou Monastery.
9-15.name: Bessarion of Larissa

9-15.bio:
St. John was a young farmer from Sfakia in Crete who had gone to Asia Minor and was betrothed there. Tradition relates that at a festival at New Ephesus he was accused by Turks and, refusing to deny Christ, was beaten and beheaded in 1811.

He is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.desc: New Martyr John of Crete, martyred at New Ephesus under the Ottomans.
9-15.name: John the New Martyr of Crete

9-15.bio:
St. Porphyrios was an actor who, in the reign of Julian the Apostate, performed a play mocking Christian baptism before the emperor. Tradition relates that when he entered the water speaking the words of baptism he was truly enlightened and confessed himself a Christian before all.

He was tortured and beheaded for his confession. He is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.desc: Holy Martyr Porphyrios the actor, baptized on stage and martyred for Christ.
9-15.name: Porphyrios the Mime

9-15.bio:
St. Symeon was a monk of Constantinople who became Archbishop of Thessaloniki in the early fifteenth century, the last Orthodox hierarch of the city before its fall to the Ottomans. He is remembered above all for his writings on the Divine Liturgy and the sacraments, which remain a chief source for the understanding of Orthodox worship, and for his pastoral care of a besieged city.

He reposed in 1429 and is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.desc: St. Symeon, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, liturgist and theologian.
9-15.name: Symeon of Thessaloniki

9-15.bio:
St. Joseph was born in Dalmatia in the sixteenth century and became a monk on Mount Athos, where he lived for many years at Vatopedi and other monasteries. In old age he was made Metropolitan of Timisoara in the Banat and later withdrew to the monastery of Partos, where he reposed.

He is honored by the Romanian Church and is commemorated on September 15.
9-15.desc: St. Joseph the New of Partos, Metropolitan of Timisoara.
9-15.name: Joseph the New of Partos

9-16.bio:
St. Euphemia the All-Praised was a virgin of Chalcedon who suffered martyrdom during the persecution under Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. Refusing to join in pagan sacrifice, she endured many tortures and committed her soul to God, receiving the crown of martyrdom in her native city.

A century and a half later, the Fourth Ecumenical Council met at Chalcedon beside her relics, and the Church honors her as a seal and confirmation of the Orthodox confession. Her chief feast is kept on September 16.
9-16.desc: Holy Great Martyr Euphemia the All-Praised of Chalcedon.
9-16.name: Euphemia the All-Praised (2nd)

9-16.bio:
St. Melitini was a Christian woman of Marcianopolis in Thrace who confessed Christ in the second century under the governor Antiochus. Tradition relates that by her prayer the idols fell to the ground, and that the governor's wife was converted by her witness.

She was beheaded, and her relics were carried to the island of Lemnos. She is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: Holy Martyr Melitini of Marcianopolis in Thrace.
9-16.name: Melitini of Marcianopolis

9-16.bio:
St. Ludmila was a princess of Bohemia baptized, according to tradition, by St. Methodius, and with her husband Borivoj she spread the Christian faith among the Czechs. She raised her grandson St. Wenceslaus in piety.

Her pagan daughter-in-law Drahomira, resenting her influence, had her strangled in her castle at Tetin in 921. She is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: Holy Martyr Ludmila, princess of Bohemia and grandmother of St. Wenceslaus.
9-16.name: Ludmila of Bohemia

9-16.bio:
St. Dorotheos was a hermit of the Egyptian desert in the fourth century who spent some sixty years in a cell near Alexandria, gathering stones in the heat of the day to build cells for other monks and eating only a little bread and herbs. His disciple Palladius recorded his life.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: Venerable Dorotheos, hermit of the Egyptian desert.
9-16.name: Dorotheos the Hermit of Egypt

9-16.bio:
St. Cyprian was born at Tarnovo in Bulgaria in the fourteenth century and lived as a monk on Mount Athos and at Constantinople, a disciple of the hesychast Patriarch Philotheos. Sent as metropolitan to Kiev and later received in Moscow, he labored to unite the Russian Church and enriched it with liturgical translations and hesychast teaching.

He reposed in 1406 and is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: St. Cyprian, Metropolitan of Kiev and Moscow, Athonite and hesychast.
9-16.name: Cyprian of Kiev and Moscow

9-16.bio:
St. Basil was bishop of Gortyna in Crete in the eighth century, in the days of the iconoclast controversy. He is remembered for his defense of the veneration of the holy icons and his care for his flock.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: St. Basil, bishop of Gortyna in Crete.
9-16.name: Basil of Gortyna

9-16.bio:
St. Ninian was a Briton of the fourth and fifth centuries who, tradition relates, studied in Rome and was sent as bishop to his people. He built a stone church at Whithorn in Galloway, called Candida Casa, and from it preached Christ to the southern Picts.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 16.
9-16.desc: St. Ninian, bishop and apostle of the southern Picts.
9-16.name: Ninian of Whithorn

9-17.bio:
St. Sophia was a pious widow of Rome in the second century who raised her three young daughters, Faith, Hope, and Love, in devotion to Christ. During the persecution under the Emperor Hadrian the three girls confessed the faith one after another and were put to death before their mother's eyes, and Sophia, having buried them, soon followed them in death from her grief.

Their names — in Greek Sophia, Pistis, Elpis, and Agapi — embody wisdom and the three great virtues, and they are beloved patrons of countless women who bear them. They are commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Faith, Hope, Love and their mother Sophia.
9-17.name: Sophia and Faith, Hope, Love

9-17.bio:
St. Agathokleia was a Christian servant in the household of a pagan couple, Nicholas and Paulina. Tradition relates that her mistress tormented her for years to make her deny Christ, and at last, unable to break her, put her to death.

She is commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Holy Martyr Agathokleia, servant girl who suffered for Christ.
9-17.name: Agathokleia the Martyr

9-17.bio:
St. Theodoti was a wealthy Christian woman of Cappadocia who confessed Christ at Nicaea in the third century. Tradition relates that she endured long imprisonment and many torments before she was beheaded.

She is commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Holy Martyr Theodoti of Cappadocia, martyred at Nicaea.
9-17.name: Theodoti of Nicaea

9-17.bio:
The holy martyrs Maximos, Theodotos and Asklepiodoti were leading Christians of Adrianople in Thrace who suffered in the persecution of the early fourth century. Tradition relates that they were brought before the emperor Maximian himself, endured many torments, and were beheaded.

They are commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Maximos, Theodotos and Asklepiodoti of Adrianople.
9-17.name: Maximos, Theodotos and Asklepiodoti

9-17.bio:
St. Lucia was a Roman widow of advanced years who confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian. Tradition relates that her own son denounced her, and that Geminianus, moved by her constancy, believed and was baptized and suffered with her.

They were beheaded together and are commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Lucia the widow of Rome and Geminianus.
9-17.name: Lucia the Widow and Geminianus

9-17.bio:
The bishops Peleus and Nilus, the priest Zeno and the noblemen Patermouthios and Elias led a great company of Egyptian and Palestinian Christians who, condemned to the mines of Palestine in the persecution of the early fourth century, were at last put to death by fire and the sword.

They are commemorated on September 17.
9-17.desc: Hieromartyrs Peleus and Nilus, bishops of Egypt, with Patermouthios, Elias and 156 martyrs of Palestine.
9-17.greek: Πηλέας, Νείλος και οι συν αυτοίς
9-17.name: Peleus, Nilus and the 156 Martyrs of Palestine

9-17.bio:
St. Herakleidios was a native of Cyprus who, according to tradition, guided the Apostles Paul and Barnabas across the island and was ordained by them bishop of Tamassos, the first in that see. He labored to bring the Cypriots to Christ, and his disciple Myron succeeded him as bishop.

The monastery of St. Herakleidios near Politiko keeps their relics. They are commemorated together on September 17.
9-17.desc: Sts. Herakleidios and Myron, bishops of Tamassos in Cyprus.
9-17.name: Herakleidios and Myron of Tamassos

9-18.bio:
St. Eumenios was Bishop of Gortyna in Crete, a shepherd remembered for his gentleness, his generosity to the poor, and his gift of wonderworking. He defended the Orthodox faith of the Church and ended his days in exile in the Thebaid of Egypt, from whence his relics were returned to his flock in Crete.

He is honored among the holy hierarchs of the Cretan church, and is commemorated on September 18.
9-18.name: Eumenios of Gortyna

9-18.bio:
St. Ariadne was a slave in the household of a prominent man of Prymnessos in Phrygia in the second century. When she refused to join in a pagan sacrifice for her master's son she was beaten and fled to the mountains; tradition relates that a rock opened to hide her from her pursuers and that she gave up her soul there.

She is commemorated on September 18, a name day for Ariadne.
9-18.desc: Holy Martyr Ariadne of Phrygia, slave girl who confessed Christ.
9-18.name: Ariadne of Phrygia

9-18.bio:
The holy martyrs Sophia and Irene were Christian women of Egypt who confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and were beheaded.

They are commemorated on September 18.
9-18.desc: Holy Martyrs Sophia and Irene of Egypt.
9-18.name: Sophia and Irene of Egypt

9-18.bio:
St. Kastor was a Christian of Alexandria who confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and, tradition relates, was put to death by torments together with the holy women Sophia and Irene.

He is commemorated on September 18.
9-18.name: Kastor the Martyr

9-18.bio:
St. Romylos was born at Vidin in Bulgaria in the fourteenth century and became a disciple of St. Gregory of Sinai at Paroria, later living as a hesychast on Mount Athos. Driven from the Holy Mountain by Turkish raids, he settled at the monastery of Ravanica in Serbia, where he reposed.

His life was written by his disciple Gregory. He is commemorated on September 18.
9-18.desc: Venerable Romylos of Ravanica, Athonite hesychast and disciple of St. Gregory of Sinai.
9-18.name: Romylos of Ravanica

9-18.bio:
St. Hilarion was born in 1805 and, after years of caring for the poor in the world, entered Optina Monastery, where he became a disciple of the elder Macarius and later confessor and elder of the community. He was known for his gentleness and his gift of healing souls afflicted by despair.

He reposed in 1873 and is numbered among the Elders of Optina. He is commemorated on September 18.
9-18.desc: Venerable Hilarion, elder of Optina Monastery.
9-18.name: Hilarion of Optina

9-19.bio:
St. Trophimos was an early confessor of Christ who suffered in Asia Minor during the persecutions of the third century, together with his companions Sabbatios and Dorymedon. Refusing to take part in pagan festivity, they confessed the faith before their judges and endured torture and death for the name of Christ.

The three martyrs are honored together as faithful witnesses who preferred the eternal joy of Christ to the passing pleasures of the world. They are commemorated on September 19.
9-19.name: Trophimos the Apostle

9-19.bio:
St. Theodore was a Greek monk born at Tarsus in Cilicia who was living in Rome when, in 668, he was consecrated Archbishop of Canterbury at an advanced age. He organized the dioceses of England, founded a school at Canterbury where Greek and Latin learning flourished, and united the English Church under one order.

He reposed in 690 and is commemorated on September 19.
9-19.desc: St. Theodore of Tarsus, Greek monk who became Archbishop of Canterbury.
9-19.name: Theodore of Tarsus, Archbishop of Canterbury

9-19.bio:
St. Theodore was a prince of Smolensk and Yaroslavl in the thirteenth century, in the years of the Mongol yoke, who ruled with justice and built churches in his lands, and received the monastic tonsure before his death in 1299. His sons David and Constantine followed him in piety.

Their relics were found incorrupt in 1463, and they are commemorated together on September 19.
9-19.desc: Holy Prince Theodore of Smolensk and Yaroslavl and his sons David and Constantine.
9-19.name: Theodore of Smolensk and his sons David and Constantine

9-19.bio:
St. Zosimas was a hermit of Cilicia in the fourth century who lived in the wilderness in such purity that, tradition relates, the wild beasts came to him without fear. Found by a hunting party of the governor and brought before him, he confessed Christ and endured torments.

He is commemorated on September 19.
9-19.desc: Venerable Zosimas the hermit of Cilicia, who lived at peace with the wild beasts.
9-19.name: Zosimas the Hermit of Cilicia

9-2.bio:
St. Mamas was a young shepherd of Caesarea in Cappadocia, born to parents who had themselves suffered imprisonment for Christ. Living simply in the hills with his flock, he confessed the faith openly during the persecutions of the third century and endured torture and death rather than deny his Lord.

He has been venerated from ancient times as a protector of shepherds and their flocks, and churches in his honor spread throughout Cappadocia, Cyprus, and Greece. He is commemorated on September 2.
9-2.name: Mamas

9-2.bio:
St. John IV, called the Faster, was a goldsmith of Constantinople who embraced the monastic life and rose, against his own wishes, to the patriarchal throne in 582. He was famed for his extreme fasting, his almsgiving, and his gift of healing, and he composed canons of penance that were long used in the Church.

He reposed in 595, leaving nothing behind but a wooden bed, a coarse blanket and a threadbare cloak. He is commemorated on September 2.
9-2.desc: St. John the Faster, Patriarch of Constantinople, renowned for his ascetic fasting.
9-2.name: John the Faster of Constantinople

9-2.bio:
St. Theodosius was born near Kiev in the eleventh century and from youth longed for the monastic life, fleeing his mother's opposition to join St. Anthony in the caves above the Dnieper. He became abbot of the Kiev Caves and gave the brotherhood the cenobitic rule of the Studion monastery.

He is honored as the founder of communal monasticism in Rus', a father of the poor and a fearless counselor of princes. He reposed in 1074; the Greek calendar keeps his memory on September 2.
9-2.desc: Venerable Theodosius, abbot of the Kiev Caves Lavra and father of Russian monasticism.
9-2.name: Theodosius of the Kiev Caves

9-2.bio:
The holy martyrs Diomedes, Julian, Philip, Eutychian, Hesychius, Leonides, Eutychius, Philadelphus, Melanippus and the holy woman Parthagape suffered together for Christ in the time of the pagan persecutions. Tradition relates that they were put to death by various torments, some by fire and some by the sword, refusing to the end to deny the faith.

They are commemorated together on September 2.
9-2.desc: Holy Martyrs Diomedes, Julian, Philip, Eutychian, Hesychius, Leonides, Philadelphus, Melanippus and Parthagape.
9-2.name: Diomedes, Julian, Philip and those with them

9-2.bio:
The righteous Eleazar was the son of Aaron and succeeded him as high priest of Israel, serving beside Joshua in the division of the Promised Land. His son Phinehas is praised in Scripture for his zeal for the Lord, by which the plague among the people was stayed, and God granted him a covenant of everlasting priesthood.

The Church remembers these Old Testament priests on September 2.
9-2.desc: Righteous Eleazar and Phinehas, high priests of Israel, son and grandson of Aaron.
9-2.name: Eleazar and Phinehas the Righteous

9-2.bio:
St. Kosmas the Hermit is listed in the Greek Synaxarion on September 2 as an ascetic and confessor of the faith. Tradition relates that he lived in solitude and prayer and suffered for his confession of Orthodoxy, reposing in peace.

His memory is kept on September 2.
9-2.desc: Venerable Kosmas the hermit and confessor.
9-2.name: Kosmas the Hermit and Confessor

9-20.bio:
St. Eustathios, called Placidas before his baptism, was a Roman general of the second century. According to tradition he was converted while hunting, beholding a vision of the Cross between the antlers of a stag; he was baptized with his wife Theopiste and their two sons, endured the loss of all his possessions and family, and after years of trial was reunited with them.

When he refused to offer pagan sacrifice after a military victory, he and his family were martyred together. He is commemorated on September 20.
9-20.name: Eustace the Great Martyr

9-20.bio:
St. Hilarion was born at Heraklion in Crete and, tradition relates, in youth was led to deny the faith in Constantinople. Repenting, he went to Mount Athos, was tonsured at the Skete of St. Anne, and prepared himself for martyrdom under the guidance of the elders.

Returning to Constantinople, he confessed Christ before the Turkish authorities and was beheaded in 1804. He is commemorated on September 20.
9-20.desc: New Martyr Hilarion of Crete, monk of the Skete of St. Anne on Mount Athos.
9-20.name: Hilarion the New Martyr of Crete

9-20.bio:
St. Hypatios, a bishop, and St. Andrew, a priest, were monks of Lydia who defended the veneration of the holy icons under the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian in the eighth century. Tradition relates that they were tortured, their beards burned and their heads smeared with pitch, and at last beheaded.

They are commemorated on September 20.
9-20.desc: Hieromartyrs Hypatios the bishop and Andrew the presbyter, confessors of the holy icons.
9-20.name: Hypatios and Andrew the Confessors

9-20.bio:
On September 20 the Greek Synaxarion remembers St. Maximos the Confessor together with St. Martin, Pope of Rome, and the confessors Euprepios, the two Anastasii and Theodore, who suffered with him for the Orthodox teaching of the two wills of Christ against the Monothelites in the seventh century. Maximos, the greatest theologian of his age, was mutilated and exiled and reposed in 662.

His principal feast is kept on January 21, and this day recalls the company of confessors who shared his struggle.
9-20.desc: Commemoration of St. Maximos the Confessor, St. Martin of Rome, and the disciples Anastasios and Theodore.
9-20.name: Maximos the Confessor and his Disciples

9-20.bio:
St. Meletios was a bishop in Cyprus remembered in the Synaxarion for his holy life and his care for his flock. He reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 20.
9-20.name: Meletios of Cyprus

9-20.bio:
St. John the Stranger, called Xenos, was born at Siva in the Messara plain of Crete in the tenth century and lived as a hermit in many parts of the island, founding churches and monasteries wherever he went. Tradition relates that he traveled to Constantinople and received imperial support for his foundations.

He reposed in peace in the eleventh century and is commemorated on September 20.
9-20.desc: Venerable John the Stranger, ascetic and founder of monasteries in Crete.
9-20.name: John the Stranger of Crete

9-20.bio:
St. Eustathios was a deacon and teacher of Constantinople, one of the great scholars of the twelfth century, who became Archbishop of Thessaloniki. He labored to reform the monastic life of his diocese and remained with his people through the Norman sack of the city in 1185, of which he wrote an account.

He reposed around 1195 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1988. He is commemorated on September 20.
9-20.desc: St. Eustathios Kataphloros, Archbishop of Thessaloniki, scholar and shepherd.
9-20.name: Eustathios of Thessaloniki

9-21.bio:
St. Quadratus was an apostle of the early Church who preached the Gospel in Athens and in Magnesia, bringing many to the faith of Christ. Tradition associates him with a written defense of the Christians presented to the emperor, one of the earliest apologies for the faith, and he ended his life as a confessor of Christ.

He is honored among the apostolic men who carried the Gospel through Greece and Asia Minor in the generations after the apostles. He is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.name: Quadratos the Apostle

9-21.bio:
The holy Prophet Jonah, son of Amittai, was sent by God to preach repentance to Nineveh. Fleeing his commission by sea, he was cast overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and after three days was delivered to complete his mission, at which the whole city repented in sackcloth.

The Lord Himself named the sign of Jonah as a figure of His own three days in the tomb. The prophet is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.desc: Holy Prophet Jonah, who preached repentance to Nineveh.
9-21.name: Jonah the Prophet

9-21.bio:
St. Jonah was a priest of Palestine in the eighth and ninth centuries who, after raising his sons Theophanes and Theodore, the Branded Confessors of the iconoclast period, entered the Lavra of St. Sabbas and lived there in asceticism. He was graced with the gift of healing.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.desc: Venerable Jonah the Presbyter of the Lavra of St. Sabbas, father of Sts. Theophanes and Theodore Graptoi.
9-21.name: Jonah the Sabbaite

9-21.bio:
The holy martyrs Eusebios, Nestabos and Zeno were brothers of Gaza who were seized by a pagan mob in the reign of Julian the Apostate and killed, with their kinsman Nestor. Bousiris, a Christian of the same city, confessed Christ and died of his torments.

They are commemorated on September 21.
9-21.desc: Holy Martyrs Eusebios, Nestabos and Zeno, brothers of Gaza, with Nestor and Bousiris.
9-21.name: Eusebios, Nestabos, Zeno and those with them

9-21.bio:
St. Isaakios was a bishop in Cyprus remembered in the Synaxarion for his holy life. He reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.name: Isaakios of Cyprus

9-21.bio:
St. Bassa was a Christian woman who confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and was put to death for the faith.

She is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.name: Bassa the Martyr

9-21.bio:
St. Platon Aivazidis was a Pontic Greek priest and archimandrite of Amisos, the present Samsun, who served the Greek Orthodox of Pontus during the years of persecution. In 1921 he was arrested with other leaders of the community and hanged at Amasya.

He was glorified by the Church of Greece among the martyrs of Asia Minor and is commemorated on September 21.
9-21.desc: Hieromartyr Platon Aivazidis, archimandrite of Amisos, martyred in 1921.
9-21.name: Platon Aivazidis

9-22.bio:
St. Phokas was a humble gardener of Sinope on the Black Sea who lived by the labor of his hands, sharing his produce with the poor and offering hospitality to travelers. When soldiers were sent to execute him for being a Christian, he received them as guests, and having prepared them supper and dug his own grave, he revealed himself in the morning and met death with peace.

He has been venerated from ancient times as a patron of gardeners and of seafarers. He is commemorated on September 22.
9-22.name: Phokas the Gardener (2nd)

9-22.bio:
St. Phokas was bishop of Sinope on the Black Sea in the time of the emperor Trajan, known for his miracles and for converting many pagans. Brought before the governor Africanus, he refused to sacrifice and was tortured and cast into a bath of scalding water, where he gave up his soul.

He is honored as a protector of sailors and is commemorated on September 22.
9-22.desc: Hieromartyr Phokas, bishop of Sinope and wonderworker.
9-22.name: Phokas of Sinope

9-22.bio:
The holy martyrs Isaac and Martin confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and were beheaded for the faith.

They are commemorated on September 22.
9-22.name: Isaac and Martin the Martyrs

9-22.bio:
St. Kosmas was a Bulgarian nobleman who fled a worldly marriage to become a monk at the monastery of Zographou on Mount Athos, where he served as ecclesiarch before withdrawing to a cave in solitude. Tradition relates that he was granted visions of the Mother of God and the gift of discernment.

He reposed in 1323 and is commemorated on September 22.
9-22.desc: Venerable Kosmas the Bulgarian, hermit of Zographou on Mount Athos.
9-22.name: Kosmas of Zographou

9-22.bio:
In the years after the Council of Lyons, when the emperor Michael VIII sought to impose union with Rome on the Church, Latin-minded troops came to Mount Athos. The abbot Thomas and twenty-five monks of Zographou, warned according to tradition by a voice from an icon of the Theotokos, refused to accept the union and shut themselves in the monastery tower, where they were burned alive in 1275.

They are commemorated on September 22 and again on October 10.
9-22.desc: The twenty-six monastic martyrs of Zographou, burned in their tower for refusing the Union of Lyons.
9-22.name: 26 Martyrs of Zographou

9-22.bio:
Blessed Paraskeva was born a serf in the early nineteenth century and, after years of hardship, took up the life of a fool for Christ in the forests of Sarov, later living at the Diveyevo convent founded by St. Seraphim. She was known throughout Russia for her clairvoyance, and the emperor Nicholas II visited her at the glorification of St. Seraphim in 1903.

She reposed in 1915 and is commemorated on September 22.
9-22.desc: Blessed Paraskeva, called Pasha of Sarov, fool for Christ of Diveyevo.
9-22.name: Paraskeva of Sarov and Diveyevo

9-23.bio:
On September 23 the Church commemorates the conception of St. John the Forerunner. As the priest Zacharias served in the Temple, the Archangel Gabriel appeared to him at the altar of incense, announcing that his prayer was heard and that his wife Elizabeth, barren and advanced in years, would bear a son who would go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah. Because Zacharias doubted, he was left mute until the child was born.

The feast celebrates the power of God who overcomes barrenness and prepares His forerunner, and it opens the cycle of feasts of the Baptist that runs through the church year.
9-23.desc: Conception of the Holy Forerunner John the Baptist.
9-23.name: Conception of John the Baptist

9-23.bio:
Sts. Xanthippe and Polyxene were sisters of Spain in the apostolic age. Tradition relates that Xanthippe, wife of a governor, received the faith from the Apostle Paul when he preached in Spain, and that Polyxene, carried off to the East, was baptized by the Apostle Andrew and returned to Spain with the Apostle Onesimos.

They lived in virginity and prayer to the end of their lives and are commemorated together on September 23, a name day for Polyxeni.
9-23.desc: Venerable Xanthippe and Polyxene, sisters of Spain, disciples of the Apostles.
9-23.name: Xanthippe and Polyxene

9-23.bio:
St. Rais was a young Christian woman of Alexandria who, seeing a company of Christians in chains being led to the ship that would carry them to trial, freely joined them and confessed Christ. She was beheaded with them in Egypt in the persecution of the early fourth century.

She is commemorated on September 23.
9-23.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Rais of Alexandria.
9-23.name: Rais of Alexandria

9-23.bio:
St. Nicholas was a youth of Karpenisi who worked in his father's grocery in Constantinople. Tradition relates that a Turkish teacher, to whom he went for lessons, tricked him into pronouncing the Muslim confession and then denounced him; before the judge Nicholas denied that he had ever left Christ.

He was beheaded in 1672, at the age of fifteen, and is commemorated on September 23.
9-23.desc: New Martyr Nicholas the grocer of Karpenisi, martyred in Constantinople.
9-23.name: Nicholas the Grocer of Karpenisi

9-23.bio:
The holy martyrs Andrew, John and John's young sons Peter and Antony were Christians of Syracuse in Sicily taken captive when the city fell to the Saracens in the ninth century. Carried to Africa, they refused to renounce Christ and were put to death by the ruler Ibrahim.

They are commemorated on September 23.
9-23.desc: Holy Martyrs Andrew and John, and John's sons Peter and Antony, of Syracuse, martyred in Africa.
9-23.name: Andrew, John, Peter and Antony of Syracuse

9-23.bio:
St. John was born a Muslim at Konitsa in Epirus, the son of a dervish, and served in the army of Ali Pasha. Coming to believe in Christ, he was baptized and lived as a farmer near Vrachori, the present Agrinio, where he was recognized, arrested and, refusing to return to Islam, beheaded in 1814.

He is commemorated on September 23.
9-23.desc: New Martyr John of Konitsa, convert from Islam, martyred at Vrachori.
9-23.name: John the New Martyr of Konitsa

9-24.bio:
St. Thekla of Iconium was converted as a young woman by the preaching of the Apostle Paul. Renouncing her betrothal to follow Christ, she was condemned to fire and to wild beasts, but tradition relates that God preserved her unharmed; she then labored in preaching and prayer, ending her long life in asceticism near Seleucia.

The Church honors her as protomartyr among women and equal-to-the-apostles, first of countless women to embrace the way of virginity for Christ. She is commemorated on September 24.
9-24.name: Thekla Equal-to-the-Apostles

9-24.bio:
St. Silouan was born a Russian peasant in 1866 and came to the monastery of St. Panteleimon on Mount Athos as a young man, where he lived for nearly fifty years in obedience and prayer. He was granted a vision of the living Christ and taught, from long struggle with despair, the word he received: keep thy mind in hell and despair not.

His writings, gathered by his disciple Archimandrite Sophrony, have made him one of the most beloved saints of the modern Church. He reposed in 1938 and is commemorated on September 24.
9-24.desc: Venerable Silouan the Athonite, monk of St. Panteleimon Monastery and teacher of prayer for the whole world.
9-24.name: Silouan the Athonite

9-24.bio:
St. Kopris was found as a newborn on a dung-heap, from which he took his name, during a raid on the monastery of St. Theodosios in Palestine, and was raised by the monks. He lived there in humility his whole life and reposed in peace in old age.

He is commemorated on September 24.
9-24.desc: Venerable Kopris of the monastery of St. Theodosios in Palestine.
9-24.name: Kopris of Palestine

9-24.bio:
St. Persis was a Christian woman who confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and, tradition relates, was cast into the sea for the faith.

She is commemorated on September 24.
9-24.name: Persis the Martyr

9-24.bio:
St. Stephen was the son of St. Symeon the Myrrh-streaming and brother of St. Sava, and the first crowned king of Serbia. He ruled with justice, built churches and monasteries including Zica, and before his death received the monastic tonsure with the name Simon.

He reposed in 1228 and his relics rest at Studenica. He is commemorated on September 24.
9-24.desc: Holy King Stephen the First-Crowned of Serbia, in monasticism Simon.
9-24.name: Stephen the First-Crowned of Serbia

9-25.bio:
St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria lived in the fifth century. The daughter of a wealthy and pious father, she fled a marriage arranged for her and, disguising herself in men's clothing, entered a monastery of men under the name Smaragdos, where she lived for many years in fasting, prayer, and perfect obscurity.

Only at the end of her life did she reveal herself to her own father, who had long mourned her and who himself took up the monastic life in her cell. She is commemorated on September 25.
9-25.name: Euphrosyne of Alexandria (2nd)

9-25.bio:
St. Paphnutius was a wealthy Christian of Alexandria in the fifth century whose only daughter Euphrosyne fled a worldly marriage to live in disguise as a monk. Tradition relates that he sought her for years, was consoled by the monk Smaragdus without knowing it was she, and learned the truth only at her deathbed.

He then took up her cell and lived there in asceticism until his own repose. He is commemorated with his daughter on September 25.
9-25.desc: Venerable Paphnutius of Egypt, father of St. Euphrosyne of Alexandria.
9-25.name: Paphnutius the Egyptian

9-25.bio:
St. Sergius was born near Rostov in the early fourteenth century and, as a young man, withdrew with his brother into the forest of Radonezh, where he built a church of the Holy Trinity. The brotherhood that gathered around him became the Trinity Lavra, the spiritual heart of Russia, and his disciples founded monasteries across the land.

He blessed Prince Dmitry Donskoy before the battle of Kulikovo and reposed in 1392. His repose is commemorated on September 25.
9-25.desc: Venerable Sergius of Radonezh, abbot and wonderworker, father of Russian monasticism.
9-25.name: Sergius of Radonezh

9-25.bio:
St. Paphnutius was an ascetic and priest of Egypt who, in the persecution of Diocletian, went of his own accord before the governor and confessed Christ. Tradition relates that his constancy under torture brought many to the faith, and that five hundred and forty-six were put to death with him before he himself was crucified.

They are commemorated on September 25.
9-25.desc: Hieromartyr Paphnutius of Egypt and the 546 martyrs who suffered with him.
9-25.name: Paphnutius the Hieromartyr and the 546 with him

9-25.bio:
The holy martyrs Paul and his wife Tatta, with their sons Sabinian, Maximos, Rufus and Eugene, were Christians of Damascus who were denounced for their faith and died together under torture.

They are commemorated on September 25.
9-25.desc: Holy Martyrs Paul and Tatta of Damascus and their sons Sabinian, Maximos, Rufus and Eugene.
9-25.name: Paul, Tatta and their Children

9-25.bio:
St. Theophilos was Archbishop of Ephesus in the eighth century who defended the veneration of the holy icons against the iconoclasts and suffered exile for his confession.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 25.
9-25.desc: St. Theophilos, Archbishop of Ephesus, confessor of the holy icons.
9-25.name: Theophilos of Ephesus

9-26.bio:
On September 26 the Church commemorates the repose of St. John the Theologian, the beloved disciple of Christ, who leaned upon the breast of the Lord at the Mystical Supper and stood by His Cross, receiving the Theotokos into his care. He wrote the fourth Gospel, three epistles, and the Revelation, and shepherded the churches of Asia from Ephesus.

Alone among the apostles he was not slain, but reposed in peace at Ephesus in great old age, ceaselessly repeating his teaching: little children, love one another. His memory is kept on September 26.
9-26.desc: Repose of the Holy Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian.
9-26.name: Repose of the Evangelist John the Theologian

9-26.bio:
St. Neilos was born at Rossano in Calabria in the tenth century, when southern Italy was still Greek and Orthodox, and after a worldly youth embraced the monastic life, becoming a renowned ascetic, calligrapher and spiritual father. Driven north by Saracen raids, he founded the Greek monastery of Grottaferrata near Rome shortly before his death.

He reposed in 1004 and is commemorated on September 26.
9-26.desc: Venerable Neilos the Younger of Rossano, founder of Grottaferrata.
9-26.name: Neilos of Calabria

9-26.bio:
The righteous Gideon was a judge of Israel called by an angel of the Lord at the winepress to deliver his people from the Midianites. Assured by the sign of the fleece, he chose three hundred men by God's command and put the enemy host to flight with trumpets and torches.

The fleece wet with dew is read by the Church as a figure of the Theotokos. Gideon is commemorated on September 26, a name day for Gedeon.
9-26.desc: Righteous Gideon, judge of Israel, who overcame Midian with three hundred men.
9-26.name: Gideon the Righteous

9-26.bio:
The holy virgins Thekla, Mariamne, Martha, Mary and Ennatha were consecrated virgins of Persia, called canonical because they were enrolled in the Church's order of virgins. Tradition relates that they were denounced by an apostate priest and beheaded for Christ in the fourth century.

They are commemorated on September 26.
9-26.desc: Holy Virgin Martyrs Thekla, Mariamne, Martha, Mary and Ennatha of Persia.
9-26.greek: Θέκλα, Μαριάμνη, Μάρθα, Μαρία και Ενναθά
9-26.name: The Five Canonical Virgins

9-26.bio:
St. John the Cave-dweller lived as a hermit in a cave near the village of Sia in Cyprus, in prayer and asceticism, and reposed in peace. A church at the site keeps his memory.

He is commemorated on September 26.
9-26.desc: Venerable John the Cave-dweller of Sia in Cyprus.
9-26.name: John the Cave-dweller of Cyprus

9-26.bio:
St. Ephraim was born at Kashin in 1412 and became a disciple of St. Sabbas of Vishera near Novgorod. He founded a monastery on the shore of Lake Ilmen at Perekom, where he cut a channel to drain the marshes, and guided the brethren until his repose in 1492.

He is commemorated on September 26.
9-26.desc: Venerable Ephraim, abbot of Perekom and wonderworker of Novgorod.
9-26.name: Ephraim of Perekom

9-27.bio:
St. Kallistratos was a Christian soldier who suffered during the persecutions at the turn of the fourth century. Discovered at prayer, he confessed Christ before his commander and was cast into the sea sewn in a sack; delivered unharmed, his courage and deliverance brought forty-nine of his fellow soldiers to believe, and together they received the crown of martyrdom by the sword.

He and his companions are honored as soldiers who exchanged earthly service for the army of Christ. They are commemorated on September 27.
9-27.name: Kallistratos

9-27.bio:
St. Mark, called also John, is the kinsman of Barnabas named in the Acts and the Epistles; St. Aristarchos was the Apostle Paul's fellow prisoner and, tradition holds, bishop of Apamea in Syria; St. Zenon is the lawyer whom Paul commends to Titus, and is said to have been bishop of Diospolis.

All three are numbered among the Seventy and are commemorated together on September 27.
9-27.desc: Holy Apostles Mark, Aristarchos and Zenon of the Seventy.
9-27.name: Mark, Aristarchos and Zenon the Apostles

9-27.bio:
St. Akylina was born at Zagliveri near Thessaloniki in the eighteenth century. Tradition relates that her father, having become a Muslim, was pressed to bring his daughter to Islam; raised in the faith by her mother, she refused before the Turkish judge and was beaten to death in 1764, at the age of eighteen.

She is commemorated on September 27.
9-27.desc: New Martyr Akylina of Zagliveri near Thessaloniki, virgin martyr.
9-27.name: Akylina of Zagliveri

9-27.bio:
St. Epicharis was a Christian woman of Rome who confessed Christ in the persecution of Diocletian and, refusing to sacrifice, was tortured and beheaded.

She is commemorated on September 27.
9-27.name: Epicharis of Rome

9-27.bio:
St. Ignatius was born in Cappadocia in the tenth century and became abbot of the monastery of Christ the Savior called Bathys Ryax, the Deep Stream. Tradition relates that he restored the monastery and was known for his humility and miracles.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 27.
9-27.desc: Venerable Ignatius, abbot of the Monastery of Christ the Savior in Cappadocia.
9-27.name: Ignatius of the Monastery of the Savior

9-27.bio:
St. Peter, Metropolitan of Krutitsa, was named locum tenens of the Patriarchal throne of Moscow after the death of St. Tikhon in 1925. Arrested by the Soviet authorities within the year, he spent the rest of his life in prisons and exile, refusing every offer of freedom in exchange for surrendering the Church's independence.

He was shot in 1937 and was glorified among the New Martyrs of Russia. He is commemorated on September 27.
9-27.desc: Hieromartyr Peter of Krutitsa, locum tenens of the Patriarchal throne of Moscow, martyred in 1937.
9-27.name: Peter of Krutitsa

9-27.bio:
St. Sabbatius was a monk of the Kirillov monastery and of Valaam who, seeking greater solitude, went with the monk Herman to the uninhabited island of Solovki in the White Sea in 1429. He lived there in prayer for several years and reposed on the mainland in 1435, and his disciples afterward founded the great Solovki monastery.

He is commemorated on September 27.
9-27.desc: Venerable Sabbatius, wonderworker of Solovki, first hermit of the White Sea island.
9-27.name: Sabbatius of Solovki

9-28.bio:
St. Chariton was a Christian of Iconium who confessed Christ under torture during the persecutions of the third century, earning the title of Confessor. Released when the persecution abated, he withdrew to the desert of Judea, where he founded some of the earliest monastic communities of Palestine and guided many souls in the ascetic life.

He is honored as a father of Palestinian monasticism, whose lavras nurtured generations of desert saints. He is commemorated on September 28.
9-28.name: Chariton the Confessor

9-28.bio:
The holy Prophet Baruch, son of Neriah, was the faithful scribe and companion of the Prophet Jeremiah, writing down his prophecies and reading them before the people and the king. He shared the prophet's sufferings at the fall of Jerusalem and went with him into Egypt.

The book that bears his name is read in the Church at the Nativity of Christ. He is commemorated on September 28.
9-28.desc: Holy Prophet Baruch, disciple and scribe of the Prophet Jeremiah.
9-28.name: Baruch the Prophet

9-28.bio:
St. Isaac the Syrian was born in the region of Qatar in the seventh century and became a monk, and for a short time bishop of Nineveh, before withdrawing to the mountains of Persia to live as a hermit. His ascetical homilies, translated into Greek at the Lavra of St. Sabbas, became one of the most cherished spiritual books of the Orthodox Church, teaching the love of God for all creation and the way of humility and prayer.

The Greek Synaxarion keeps his memory on September 28; he is also honored on January 28.
9-28.desc: Venerable Isaac the Syrian, bishop of Nineveh and teacher of the inner life.
9-28.name: Isaac the Syrian

9-28.bio:
St. Wenceslaus was raised by his grandmother St. Ludmila and became prince of Bohemia while still young, ruling with justice, building churches, and caring for the poor with his own hands. His pagan-minded brother Boleslav, envying his rule and hating his faith, invited him to a feast and killed him at the church door in 935.

He is the patron of the Czech people and is commemorated on September 28.
9-28.desc: Holy Martyr Wenceslaus, prince of the Czechs.
9-28.name: Wenceslaus of Bohemia

9-28.bio:
St. Auxentios was one of the company of monks who, according to Cypriot tradition, came to the island from Palestine and lived as hermits in its mountains and caves. He is venerated in the region of Karpasia, where a church keeps his memory.

He is commemorated on September 28.
9-28.desc: Venerable Auxentios, monk and ascetic of Cyprus.
9-28.name: Auxentios of Cyprus

9-28.bio:
In the persecution of Diocletian, Mark, a shepherd of Antioch in Pisidia, was seized for his faith; tradition relates that the brothers Alexander, Alphaeus and Zosimas, ordered to forge instruments of torture for him, were converted and suffered with him, together with Nikon, Neon, Heliodoros and many others.

They are commemorated together on September 28.
9-28.desc: Holy Martyrs Mark the shepherd, Alexander, Alphaeus, Zosimas and the thirty martyrs of Pisidia and Phrygia.
9-28.name: Alexander and the 30 Martyrs

9-29.bio:
St. Cyriacus the Hermit was a Palestinian ascetic of the fifth and sixth centuries. Coming to the Holy Land as a young man, he passed his long life in the desert of Judea in the communities founded by the great desert fathers, advancing ever deeper into solitude, fasting, and unceasing prayer, and attaining great old age.

He was a firm defender of the Orthodox faith against the errors of his time, and many sought out his counsel in the wilderness. He is commemorated on September 29.
9-29.name: Cyriac the Hermit

9-29.bio:
St. Malachi was born at Lindos on Rhodes and became a monk in Jerusalem, where he served the Holy Sepulchre. Tradition relates that he was accused before the Turkish authorities of insulting Islam and, refusing to convert, was tortured and put to death in 1500.

He is commemorated on September 29.
9-29.desc: New Martyr Malachi of Rhodes, monk martyred in Jerusalem.
9-29.name: Malachi the New Martyr of Rhodes

9-29.bio:
St. Petronia was a Christian woman who confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions and was beheaded for the faith.

She is commemorated on September 29.
9-29.name: Petronia the Martyr

9-29.bio:
St. Dadas was a kinsman of the Persian king Shapur and governor of a province who was found to be a Christian and handed over to torture. Tradition relates that the king's own son Gobdelaas, sent to preside at the trial, was converted by the miracles he witnessed, as was his sister Kasdoa, and that they suffered with Dadas and Kasdoos.

They are commemorated on September 29.
9-29.desc: Holy Martyrs Dadas, Gobdelaas, Kasdoos and Kasdoa of Persia.
9-29.name: Gobdelaas, Dadas, Kasdoos and Kasdoa

9-29.bio:
St. Theophanes was a Christian of Gaza who spent all he had on the poor, the sick and strangers, until he fell into poverty himself and bore illness with patience. Tradition relates that after his death a healing myrrh flowed from his tomb.

He is commemorated on September 29.
9-29.desc: Righteous Theophanes the Merciful of Gaza.
9-29.name: Theophanes the Merciful of Gaza

9-29.bio:
The Church of Aetolia keeps the memory of three Christians of Vrachori, the present Agrinio, who were put to death by the Ottomans for refusing to deny Christ. Their names are not preserved in the Synaxarion.

They are commemorated on September 29.
9-29.desc: The three New Martyrs of Vrachori, the present Agrinio, martyred under the Ottomans.
9-29.name: Three New Martyrs of Vrachori

9-3.bio:
St. Anthimos was Bishop of Nicomedia during the great persecution under Diocletian at the opening of the fourth century. When many of his flock were slain, he shepherded the survivors from hiding, strengthening them by letters and prayer, until he was discovered, confessed Christ before his judges, and was beheaded.

He is honored as a hieromartyr who laid down his life for the flock entrusted to him. He is commemorated on September 3.
9-3.name: Anthimos of Nicomedia

9-3.bio:
St. Phoebe was a deaconess of the Church at Cenchreae, the eastern port of Corinth, in the first century. The Apostle Paul commends her in his Epistle to the Romans as a servant of the Church and a helper of many, including himself, and tradition holds that she carried that epistle to Rome.

She is honored as the first deaconess named in Scripture and reposed in peace. Her memory is kept on September 3, a beloved name day in Greece.
9-3.desc: St. Phoebe the Deaconess of Cenchreae, commended by the Apostle Paul.
9-3.name: Phoebe the Deaconess

9-3.bio:
St. Theoktistos was the companion and fellow ascetic of St. Euthymios the Great in the wilderness of Judea in the fifth century. Together they found a cave in a ravine near the Dead Sea, where a monastery grew up around them; when Euthymios withdrew to deeper solitude, Theoktistos remained as abbot and spiritual father of the brethren.

He reposed in great old age, honored by all the monks of Palestine, and is commemorated on September 3.
9-3.desc: Venerable Theoktistos, fellow ascetic of St. Euthymios the Great in the Judean desert.
9-3.name: Theoktistos of Palestine

9-3.bio:
St. Polydoros was born in Nicosia, Cyprus, in the eighteenth century and worked as a merchant in Egypt, where, tradition relates, in a moment of weakness he was led to deny the faith. Overcome with remorse, he wandered from place to place seeking to confess Christ openly.

At New Ephesus in Asia Minor he declared himself a Christian before the Ottoman judge, endured imprisonment and torture, and was hanged in 1794. He is commemorated on September 3.
9-3.desc: New Martyr Polydoros of Nicosia, martyred at Ephesus under the Ottomans.
9-3.name: Polydoros the New Martyr of Cyprus

9-3.bio:
St. Vasilissa was a young girl of Nicomedia, only nine years old according to tradition, who confessed Christ during the persecution of Diocletian. Brought before the governor Alexander, she remained unshaken through beatings and fire, and the governor himself is said to have been moved to repentance.

She reposed in peace soon afterward, praying at the edge of the city. Her memory is kept on September 3.
9-3.desc: Holy Martyr Vasilissa, child martyr of Nicomedia.
9-3.name: Vasilissa of Nicomedia

9-3.bio:
St. Aristion was born of pagan parents in Syria in the early centuries of the Church and, coming to faith in Christ, was made bishop of Alexandria in Cilicia, the lesser Alexandria. He labored to bring the pagans of his region to the faith.

He was arrested for his preaching and, refusing to deny Christ, was burned alive. The Church commemorates him on September 3.
9-3.desc: Hieromartyr Aristion, bishop of Alexandria in Cilicia.
9-3.name: Aristion of Alexandria

9-30.bio:
St. Gregory, the Illuminator of Armenia, brought the Gospel to the Armenian people at the turn of the fourth century. For his confession of Christ he endured long imprisonment in a deep pit, yet through his patience and prayer King Tiridates was converted, and Gregory, consecrated bishop, baptized the king and his people, making Armenia one of the first Christian nations.

He is honored as the apostle and first hierarch of the Armenian church, and his memory is kept throughout the Orthodox world on September 30.
9-30.name: Gregory of Armenia

9-30.bio:
St. Rhipsime was a Roman virgin of great beauty who fled with her abbess Gaiane and their companions to Armenia to escape the emperor Diocletian. The Armenian king Tiridates sought her for himself and, refused, had her and her companions put to death with great cruelty around the year 300.

Tradition relates that the king was afterward struck with madness and healed by St. Gregory the Illuminator, and so Armenia came to Christ. They are commemorated with St. Gregory on September 30.
9-30.desc: Holy Virgin Martyrs Rhipsime, Gaiane and their thirty-two companions, martyred in Armenia.
9-30.name: Rhipsime, Gaiane and the Virgin Martyrs of Armenia

9-30.bio:
The holy martyrs Stratonikos and Mardonios confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions; tradition relates that Stratonikos was beheaded and Mardonios burned.

They are commemorated on September 30.
9-30.name: Stratonikos and Mardonios

9-30.bio:
St. Gregory was born of a noble family of Galich and, giving his inheritance to the poor, became a monk and later a disciple of St. Dionysius of Glushitsa. He founded a monastery on the river Pelshma in the Vologda forests and was known for rebuking princes who oppressed the people.

He reposed in 1442 and is commemorated on September 30.
9-30.desc: Venerable Gregory of Pelshma, abbot and wonderworker of Vologda.
9-30.name: Gregory of Pelshma

9-30.bio:
St. Michael, according to tradition a Syrian or Bulgarian by birth, was sent from Constantinople as the first Metropolitan of Kiev after the baptism of Prince Vladimir in 988. He baptized the people of Kiev, overthrew the idols, and established the first churches and schools of the Russian land.

He reposed in 992 and is commemorated on September 30.
9-30.desc: St. Michael, first Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus'.
9-30.name: Michael, First Metropolitan of Kiev

9-4.bio:
St. Babylas was Bishop of Antioch in the third century, remembered for his boldness in barring an emperor stained with blood from entering the church until he should repent. During the persecution under Decius he was imprisoned for his confession of Christ and died in chains around the year 253.

His relics were greatly honored in Antioch, and his memory endured as an example of a shepherd who feared God more than earthly power. He is commemorated on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Babylas, Patriarch of Antioch.
9-4.name: Babylas of Antioch

9-4.bio:
The holy Prophet Moses, of the tribe of Levi, was saved from the Nile as an infant and raised in the house of Pharaoh. Called by God from the burning bush, he led the people of Israel out of Egypt, through the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness, and received the Law on Mount Sinai, where he spoke with God face to face.

He died on Mount Nebo within sight of the Promised Land. The Church honors him as the greatest of the prophets of the Law and, with Elijah, a witness of the Transfiguration. His memory is kept on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Prophet Moses the God-seer, who led Israel out of Egypt and received the Law on Sinai.
9-4.name: Moses the Prophet and God-seer

9-4.bio:
St. Hermione was one of the four daughters of the Apostle Philip the Deacon, who are named in the Acts of the Apostles as virgins who prophesied. Tradition relates that she settled in Ephesus, practiced the art of healing, and cared freely for the sick and the poor.

She confessed Christ under the emperors Trajan and Hadrian and endured torments, reposing in peace at Ephesus. She is commemorated on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Martyr Hermione, daughter of the Apostle Philip the Deacon, prophetess and healer.
9-4.name: Hermione the Daughter of Philip

9-4.bio:
St. Anthimos the New was born on Kefalonia in the eighteenth century and lost his sight in youth. He embraced the monastic life and, though blind, traveled through the islands of the Aegean and the Ionian Sea preaching, founding monasteries and strengthening the faithful under Ottoman and Venetian rule.

He reposed in peace in 1781 and is commemorated on September 4.
9-4.desc: Venerable Anthimos the New, the blind ascetic of Kefalonia.
9-4.name: Anthimos the New of Kefalonia

9-4.bio:
St. Babylas was a Christian teacher in Nicomedia who instructed children in letters and in the faith. Denounced during the persecution of Maximian, he was brought before the governor with eighty-four of his young pupils, who refused with him to deny Christ.

After torments the teacher was beheaded, and the children were put to death after him. They are commemorated together on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Martyr Babylas, teacher of Nicomedia, and his 84 young pupils.
9-4.name: Babylas of Nicomedia and the 84 Children

9-4.bio:
Tradition relates that Theotimos and Theodoulos were executioners in the service of a pagan governor who, witnessing the constancy of the Christians they were ordered to torture, confessed Christ themselves.

They were put to death for their confession and are commemorated on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Martyrs Theotimos and Theodoulos, executioners converted by the martyrs they were sent to kill.
9-4.name: Theotimos and Theodoulos

9-4.bio:
The holy martyrs Kentyrion, Theodore, Ammianos, Julian and Oceanos were Christians of a village near Nicomedia who were seized during the persecution of Maximian. They confessed Christ before the governor and endured cruel torments before being burned to death.

They are commemorated on September 4.
9-4.desc: Holy Martyrs Kentyrion, Theodore, Ammianos, Julian and Oceanos of Nicomedia.
9-4.name: Kentyrion, Theodore, Ammianos, Julian and Oceanos

9-5.bio:
The holy Prophet Zacharias was a priest of the Temple in Jerusalem and the father of St. John the Baptist. The Archangel Gabriel announced to him at the altar of incense that his wife Elizabeth, barren and advanced in years, would bear a son; and at the child's birth Zacharias prophesied concerning the coming salvation of Israel.

Tradition holds that he was slain in the Temple for refusing to betray his son during Herod's slaughter of the infants. With righteous Elizabeth he is commemorated on September 5.
9-5.desc: Prophet Zacharias and Elizabeth, parents of John the Baptist.
9-5.name: Zacharias the Prophet

9-5.bio:
The righteous Elizabeth was of the daughters of Aaron and the wife of the priest Zacharias; the Gospel of Luke calls them both righteous before God.
