Barren and advanced in years, she conceived St. John the Forerunner by the promise of the Archangel Gabriel, and when the Virgin Mary came to visit her she was filled with the Holy Spirit and greeted her as the Mother of her Lord.

Tradition relates that during the slaughter of the innocents she fled with her infant son into the wilderness, where a rock opened to shelter them, and that she reposed there in peace. She is commemorated with her husband on September 5, a major name day in Greece.
9-5.desc: Righteous Elizabeth, wife of the Prophet Zacharias and mother of St. John the Baptist.
9-5.name: Elizabeth the Righteous, Mother of the Forerunner

9-5.bio:
St. Abdaios was a bishop in Persia in the fifth century, under King Yazdegerd. Refusing to worship the sun and fire as the Persians demanded, he was beaten with thorny rods and died of his wounds, giving thanks to God.

He is commemorated on September 5.
9-5.name: Abdaios of Persia

9-5.bio:
The holy martyrs Medimnos, Urban and Theodore, with some eighty priests and deacons of Constantinople, went to the Arian emperor Valens to plead for the Orthodox who were being persecuted. The emperor ordered them put aboard a ship, which was set on fire at sea, and all perished in the flames near Nicomedia.

They are commemorated on September 5.
9-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Medimnos, Urban, Theodore and eighty clergy of Constantinople burned at sea under the Arian emperor Valens.
9-5.name: Medimnos, Urban, Theodore and the 77 with them

9-5.bio:
St. Athanasius was a learned monk and abbot of the monastery of St. Simeon at Brest in the seventeenth century, when the Orthodox of Lithuania and Poland were under pressure to accept the Union with Rome. He defended the Orthodox faith fearlessly before the Polish authorities and endured repeated imprisonment.

In 1648 he was seized, tortured, and shot, and his body was cast into a pit; his relics were later recovered incorrupt. He is commemorated on September 5.
9-5.desc: Hieromartyr Athanasius, abbot of Brest, martyred for Orthodoxy in 1648.
9-5.name: Athanasius of Brest

9-6.bio:
This feast commemorates the miracle wrought by the Archangel Michael at Chonae in Asia Minor. According to tradition, pagans sought to destroy a church and healing spring dedicated to the Archangel by turning rivers against it; at the prayer of the devout sacristan Archippos, the Archangel appeared, struck the rock with his staff, and channeled the waters harmlessly into a chasm, preserving the holy place.

The Church keeps the memory of this wonder on September 6, honoring the Archangel Michael as protector of the faithful and captain of the heavenly hosts, whose chief feast with the Archangel Gabriel follows on November 8.
9-6.desc: Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Chonae.
9-6.name: Miracle of Archangel Michael at Chonae

9-6.bio:
St. Eudoxios was a military commander of Melitene in Armenia in the time of the persecutions of Diocletian and his successors. When he declared himself a Christian, tradition relates that more than a thousand soldiers under him laid down their arms and confessed with him, and were put to death together. Eudoxios, with his friends Zeno and Makarios, was beheaded.

St. Romylos, an officer of the emperor Trajan's court, was likewise martyred for rebuking the emperor's persecution of Christian soldiers. They are commemorated together on September 6.
9-6.desc: Holy Martyrs Eudoxios, Romylos, Zeno and Makarios, and the many soldiers martyred with them.
9-6.name: Eudoxios, Romylos, Zeno and Makarios

9-6.bio:
St. Kalodoti was a Christian woman of Alexandria who suffered martyrdom in the persecution of Decius in the third century, together with the priest Faustus, the deacon Abibas and their companions.

She is commemorated on September 6.
9-6.name: Kalodoti of Alexandria

9-6.bio:
The holy martyrs Faustus the presbyter, Abibas the deacon, Kyriakos, Dionysios, Andrew, Theoktistos the ship captain, Sarapabon the senator and their companions confessed Christ at Alexandria in the persecution of Decius. Brought before the governor Valerius, they refused to sacrifice and were put to death by various torments.

They are commemorated on September 6.
9-6.desc: Holy Martyrs Faustus the presbyter, Abibas the deacon, Kyriakos and their companions at Alexandria.
9-6.name: Faustus, Abibas, Kyriakos and those with them

9-6.bio:
St. Archippos came as a boy to serve at the church of the Archangel Michael at Chonae in Phrygia, where a healing spring flowed, and lived there for many decades in fasting and prayer. When pagans diverted two rivers to sweep away the church, he prayed without ceasing, and the Archangel appeared and split the rock so that the waters were swallowed up.

He reposed in peace in old age at the shrine he had guarded. He is commemorated on September 6, the day of the Miracle at Chonae.
9-6.desc: Venerable Archippos, sacristan of the church of the Archangel Michael at Chonae.
9-6.name: Archippos of Chonae

9-6.bio:
St. Lygeri was a young Christian woman of Chios in the Ottoman period. Tradition relates that, pursued by a Turk who sought to make her his wife and change her faith, she refused steadfastly and was put to death for her confession of Christ.

She is honored among the saints of Chios and commemorated on September 6.
9-6.desc: New Martyr Lygeri of Chios, virgin martyr under the Ottomans.
9-6.name: Lygeri the New Martyr of Chios

9-7.bio:
St. Sozon was a shepherd of Cilicia in Asia Minor who tended his flock in prayer and meditation on the Scriptures. During a time of persecution he confessed Christ boldly at Pompeiopolis, and after enduring torture he gave up his soul to God, receiving the crown of martyrdom.

His memory has been kept from early times, and a church was raised over his relics where the faithful sought healing. He is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.name: Sozont

9-7.bio:
St. Kassiani was a noblewoman of Constantinople in the ninth century, learned and pious. Tradition relates that she was among the maidens presented to the emperor Theophilos as a prospective bride and that her bold reply cost her the crown; she embraced the monastic life instead and founded a convent in the city.

She is the most celebrated woman hymnographer of the Church, and her troparion on the sinful woman who anointed the Lord is sung on Holy Tuesday evening. She is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.desc: Venerable Kassiani the Hymnographer, nun of Constantinople and author of the Hymn of Kassiani.
9-7.name: Kassiani the Hymnographer

9-7.bio:
St. Evodos was the first bishop of Antioch after the Apostle Peter, and is remembered by his successor St. Ignatius the God-bearer; tradition holds that he was martyred under Nero. St. Onesiphoros is praised by the Apostle Paul, who writes that he often refreshed him and was not ashamed of his chains, seeking him out diligently in Rome.

Both are numbered among the Seventy Apostles and commemorated together on September 7.
9-7.desc: Holy Apostles Evodos and Onesiphoros of the Seventy.
9-7.name: Evodos and Onesiphoros the Apostles

9-7.bio:
St. Eupsychios was the son of a senator of Caesarea in Cappadocia who confessed Christ in the reign of Hadrian. He was tortured and imprisoned, and tradition relates that he was healed of his wounds in prison by an angel; brought again before the governor, he was put to death by the sword.

He is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.desc: Holy Martyr Eupsychios of Caesarea in Cappadocia.
9-7.name: Eupsychios of Caesarea

9-7.bio:
St. Daniel of Katounakia was born in Smyrna in 1846 and came to Mount Athos as a young man, living for years at the monastery of St. Panteleimon and later in the desert of Katounakia, where he founded the brotherhood of the Danielaioi. He was a learned spiritual father, iconographer and writer, consulted by elders across the Holy Mountain and by St. Nektarios of Aegina.

He reposed in 1929 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2020. He is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.desc: Venerable Daniel of Katounakia, Athonite elder and founder of the Danielaioi brotherhood.
9-7.name: Daniel of Katounakia

9-7.bio:
St. John was Archbishop of Novgorod in the twelfth century, a man of prayer and a defender of his city. Tradition relates that during a siege of Novgorod he carried the icon of the Mother of God of the Sign onto the walls and the enemy was turned back, and that he was slandered and vindicated by a miracle on the river Volkhov.

He reposed in 1186 and is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.desc: St. John the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Novgorod.
9-7.name: John of Novgorod

9-7.bio:
St. Luke was born in Lycaonia and became the third abbot of the monastery of the Savior called Batheos Ryakos, the Deep Stream, near Triglia in Bithynia, a house famed for the strictness of its rule. He guided the brethren in humility and reposed in peace in the tenth century.

He is commemorated on September 7.
9-7.desc: Venerable Luke, abbot of the monastery of the Deep Stream in Bithynia.
9-7.name: Luke of Batheos Ryakos

9-8.bio:
The Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, celebrated on September 8, is the first Great Feast of the church year. According to tradition, the righteous Joachim and Anna remained childless into old age, bearing reproach with patience and prayer; God heard them and granted them a daughter, Mary, who was to become the Mother of the Saviour.

Her birth is celebrated as the dawn of salvation, the coming into the world of her through whom the Word of God would take flesh. The feast honors also the faithfulness of her parents, and is a day of joy for all who bear the names Maria and Panagiota.
9-8.desc: The Nativity of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary.
9-8.name: Nativity of the Theotokos

9-8.bio:
St. Athanasios was born at Koulakia near Thessaloniki, the present Chalastra, in the eighteenth century. Tradition relates that, having in a dispute been drawn into words the Turks took as an acceptance of Islam, he refused absolutely to deny Christ and was condemned.

He was hanged in Thessaloniki in 1774 and is commemorated on September 8.
9-8.desc: New Martyr Athanasios of Koulakia, martyred in Thessaloniki under the Ottomans.
9-8.name: Athanasios of Koulakia

9-8.bio:
The holy martyrs Rufus and Rufianus were brothers who confessed Christ during the pagan persecutions and were beheaded together.

They are commemorated on September 8, the feast of the Nativity of the Theotokos.
9-8.desc: Holy Martyrs Rufus and Rufianus, brothers beheaded for Christ.
9-8.name: Rufus and Rufianus

9-8.bio:
The holy martyrs Severus and Artemidoros confessed Christ in the time of the persecutions; tradition relates that Severus was put to death by the sword and Artemidoros by fire.

They are commemorated on September 8.
9-8.name: Severus and Artemidoros

9-8.bio:
St. Sophronios was a Greek hierarch of the eighteenth century who served as bishop of Achtala in Georgia, ministering to the Greek miners and Orthodox faithful of that region. He was known for his ascetic life and pastoral care and reposed in peace.

He is commemorated on September 8.
9-8.desc: St. Sophronios, bishop of Achtala in Georgia.
9-8.name: Sophronios of Achtala

9-9.bio:
Saints Joachim and Anne were the parents of the Most Holy Theotokos. Righteous and devout, they remained childless into old age, bearing reproach with patience and beseeching God with tears; in answer to their prayer they were granted a daughter, Mary, whom they dedicated to the Lord in His Temple.

The Church honors them as the God-bearing ancestors of Christ, and their names are invoked at the close of every Orthodox service. Their synaxis is kept on September 9, the day after the Nativity of the Theotokos.
9-9.desc: Holy and God-Bearing Ancestors Joachim and Anne, parents of the Theotokos.
9-9.name: Joachim and Anne

9-9.bio:
St. Severian was a nobleman of Sebaste in Armenia who visited and encouraged the Forty Martyrs in their prison. After their death he was himself denounced as a Christian before the governor Lysias, confessed Christ boldly, and was tortured and hanged by a stone from the city wall.

He suffered around the year 320 and is commemorated on September 9.
9-9.desc: Great Martyr Severian of Sebaste in Armenia.
9-9.name: Severian of Sebaste

9-9.bio:
The Third Ecumenical Council met at Ephesus in 431 under the presidency of St. Cyril of Alexandria. It condemned the teaching of Nestorius, who divided Christ into two persons and refused the Virgin the title Theotokos, and confirmed that Mary is truly the Mother of God, since the one born of her is the eternal Son and Word.

The Holy Fathers of the Council are commemorated on September 9, in the afterfeast of the Nativity of the Theotokos.
9-9.desc: Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the Third Ecumenical Council at Ephesus.
9-9.name: Fathers of the Third Ecumenical Council

9-9.bio:
St. Theophanes was born of pagan parents and came to Christ as a youth, fleeing to Mount Diabenos where he lived under the guidance of an elder in fasting and prayer. He later suffered for the veneration of the holy icons and is honored as a confessor.

He reposed in peace and is commemorated on September 9.
9-9.desc: Venerable Theophanes the Confessor and faster of Mount Diabenos.
9-9.name: Theophanes the Confessor of Diabenos

9-9.bio:
St. Joseph was born near Volokolamsk in 1440 and became a monk in youth under St. Paphnutius of Borovsk. He founded the monastery of the Dormition at Volokolamsk, giving it a strict cenobitic rule and making it a center of charity in times of famine, and he defended Orthodoxy against the heresy of the Judaizers.

He reposed in 1515 and is commemorated on September 9.
9-9.desc: Venerable Joseph, abbot and wonderworker of Volokolamsk.
9-9.name: Joseph of Volokolamsk

9-9.bio:
St. Ciaran was born in Connacht in the early sixth century and studied under St. Finnian of Clonard, being counted among the twelve apostles of Ireland. He founded the monastery of Clonmacnoise on the Shannon, which became one of the great centers of learning of the Irish Church.

He reposed young, in the same year as his foundation, and is commemorated on September 9.
9-9.desc: Venerable Ciaran, abbot and founder of Clonmacnoise in Ireland.
9-9.name: Ciaran of Clonmacnoise
